newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLL-NOKIA Q2 PROFIT SEEN AT FIM 1.64 BLN.
newsitem.headline: POLL-NOKIA Q2 PROFIT SEEN AT FIM 1.64 BLN.

text.p: A Reuters survey of equities
analysts showed a 1.64 billion markka median forecast for
Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy's second-quarter profit before
tax and minority interest.
Profit before tax, minorities EPS
(FIM million) (markka)
Q2 Jan-June Q2 Jan-June
(Profit forecasts by 23 analysts, EPS by 17 analysts).
Analysts were polled after Swedish telecoms group Ericsson
last week reported a 44 percent rise in H1 profits.
Nokia's Q2 and first-half results are due on August 4 at
around 1600/1300 GMT.
In Q2, 1996, Nokia's profit before tax and minorities was
728 million markka. In January-June last year, the group's
profit was 1.13 billion markka.
In Q1, Nokia posted a 1.45 billion markka profit before tax
and minorities, saying its first-quarter performance boosted
confidence for strong growth and good profitability in 1997.
The median of 22 analysts' forecasts for Nokia's full-year
1997 profit before tax and minorities was 6.8 billion markka
(range 6,125-7,595 million).
In 1996, the group's profit was 3.9 billion markka.
The median of 21 analysts' forecasts for full-year 1997 EPS
was 17.2 markka (range 15.5-19.7 markka) compared to 10.73
markka in 1996.
Contributors to the survey were Alfred Berg, AG Private
Bankers, Aktia Bank, Aros Securities, BZW Securities, Carnegie,
Den Danske Bank, Daiwa-Europe, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell,
Enskilda Securities, Evli Securities, FIM Securities,
Handelsbanken, Hagstromer&Qvinberg, Interbank, Lehman Brothers,
Merill Lynch, Merita Bank, Morgan Stanley, Opstock, Salomon
Brothers, Schroder Securities, SBC Warburg, SmithBarney and
Paribas.
